---
title: "Brian Stacy's Resume"
author: Brian Stacy
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  pagedown::html_resume:
    css: ['css/custom_resume.css', 'css/styles.css', 'resume']
    # set it to true for a self-contained HTML page but it'll take longer to render
    self_contained: true

---


```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  results='asis', 
  echo = FALSE
)
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)

# Set this to true to have links turned into footnotes at the end of the document
PDF_EXPORT <- FALSE

# Holds all the links that were inserted for placement at the end
links <- c()

source('parsing_functions.R')


# First let's get the data, filtering to only the items tagged as
# Resume items. data/positions.csv is hand-maintained (education, positions,
# teaching); data/publications_auto.csv is regenerated from ORCID + OpenAlex
# by scripts/fetch_publications.R, so new papers show up without hand-editing.
# start/end are forced to character (not guessed per-file) because
# data/positions.csv can contain "current", which would otherwise make the
# two files' column types disagree and break bind_rows().
position_cols <- cols(
  section = col_character(),
  in_resume = col_logical(),
  title = col_character(),
  loc = col_character(),
  institution = col_character(),
  start = col_character(),
  end = col_character(),
  description_1 = col_character(),
  description_2 = col_character(),
  description_3 = col_character()
)

position_data <- bind_rows(
    read_csv('data/positions.csv', col_types = position_cols),
    read_csv('data/publications_auto.csv', col_types = position_cols)
  ) %>%
  filter(in_resume) %>%
  mutate(
    # Build some custom sections by collapsing others
    section = case_when(
      section %in% c('research_positions', 'industry_positions') ~ 'positions',
      section %in% c('data_science_writings', 'by_me_press') ~ 'writings',
      TRUE ~ section
    )
  )

```
